evidence.locator: Update printed p. 4, Input Costs and Pricing; printed p. 6, Operating Margin Structure footnote (a); PDF pages 5 and 7 (exchange letter precedes update)

ranking_policy: Only the pressure passage enters first-stage ranking. Geography, identity, actions, profit, figures, unknowns and later outcomes are display-only.
episode_boundary: One Q4FY21 observation in continuing 2020-22 input inflation. Earlier/following quarters and FY21 summaries are not additional situations; true cost-pressure onset/end are unknown.
comparison_limit: India domestic FMCG, including edible and hair oils. The 17.6% operating margin is not the group margin or gross margin. Vegetable oil and copra are different purchases from diesel fuel.
unknowns: Actual consumed-input prices and inventory timing; these quoted market benchmarks can differ from purchase costs.
The India operating-profit numerator is not reconciled to statutory profit in this update.
Separate effects of price changes, cost control and changing sales mix; no independent causal estimate.
True episode boundaries and later results.

pressure.value: Copra (dried coconut kernel) and rice bran oil input prices rose. High-density polyethylene (HDPE) plastic input prices also rose.

evidence.locator: Update printed p. 4, Input Costs and Pricing; printed p. 6, Operating Margin Structure footnote (a); PDF pages 5 and 7 (exchange letter precedes update)

margin_or_profit.value: Marico reported an India operating margin of 17.6%, versus 22.8% a year earlier. This domestic profit-to-sales measure is separate from the group margin.

evidence.locator: Update printed p. 2, India Business opening paragraph; PDF page 3

other_drivers.value: The company cautioned that growth was measured against a quarter affected by lockdowns. Market commodity prices can differ from its consumed-input costs because of inventory positions.

evidence.locator: Update printed pp. 1-2, Performance Overview and India Business; printed p. 6, footnote (a)

response.value: Marico reported raising Parachute coconut-oil and Saffola edible-oil prices during the quarter and using cost controls. It attributed part of the cost offset to these actions; their separate effects are not established.

evidence.locator: Update printed p. 2, India Business, Coconut Oil and Saffola; PDF page 3

metric.name: India operating margin
metric.basis: Company-reported India operating profit as a share of domestic turnover; the update does not reconcile its profit numerator to statutory profit. This is neither gross margin nor consolidated margin.

evidence.locator: Update printed p. 2, India Business; PDF page 3

figures.name: Company-estimated pricing contribution
figures.basis: Issuer attribution in the income bridge; not an independently isolated action effect. Includes JPY7.0 billion in Japan and JPY7.0 billion outside Japan.
figures.scope: Kao strategic pricing, Japan and overseas consumer products

evidence.locator: Printed p. 15 / PDF page 15, full-year table and pricing approaches

ranking_policy: Only the pressure passage enters first-stage ranking. Geography, identity, actions, profit, figures, unknowns and later outcomes are display-only.
episode_boundary: One FY2022 observation within continuing 2021-23 material pressure. Quarterly updates and FY2023 follow-ups are not independent cases. True onset and end are unknown.
comparison_limit: Japan and overseas consumer products, not Japan alone. The negative JPY46.0 billion figure is a company-estimated year-on-year cost headwind after Chemical selling-price offsets, not an operating loss or margin. Natural fats/oils are not a fuel disclosure.
unknowns: Country-by-country material-cost amounts and purchase/hedging timing.
Isolated effects of each pricing, pack-size, promotion or cost-reduction action.
The component breakdown is charted without exact FY2022 amounts; no values were digitized or assigned to individual inputs.
Actual 2023 energy/material outcomes are outside this case; the right-hand chart bar is a forecast.
True episode boundaries and later results.

pressure.value: Natural-fat and oil input costs rose. Petrochemical raw-material and packaging costs rose; paper and cardboard costs rose.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 23 / PDF page 23, Consumer Products material-price impact chart: FY2022 bar and -46.0 versus 2021 annotation; footnote on Chemical selling-price offsets

margin_or_profit.value: Kao estimated an adverse material-price effect of 46.0 billion Japanese yen compared with 2021. This company estimate explains part of the change in operating profit and includes selling-price offsets in its Chemical business; it is not a reported operating loss or margin.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 23 / PDF page 23, Consumer Products material-price impact chart: FY2022 bar and -46.0 versus 2021 annotation; footnote on Chemical selling-price offsets; printed p. 13, income bridge and footnote 1

other_drivers.value: Kao also reported sales and business-mix changes, logistics expenses and market slowdowns. The group includes a Chemical business; its consolidated operating profit is not a Japan consumer-products result.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 13-14, operating-income bridge and Q4 forecast-versus-results discussion; PDF pages 13-14

response.value: Kao reported price increases, smaller product contents, higher-value products and changes to promotions. It estimated a pricing contribution of 14.0 billion Japanese yen, split equally between Japan and overseas; this company bridge is not independent proof of the actions’ effects.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 15 / PDF page 15, strategic price implementation and FY2022 Japan/outside-Japan table

metric.name: Estimated material-price effect on income
metric.basis: Company-estimated adverse FY2022 change versus 2021; net of selling-price adjustments in the Chemical business. The chart is rebased to 2015, but -46.0 is the 2022-versus-2021 step, not the cumulative level. Not an operating loss.
metric.scope: Kao Consumer Products material-cost bridge, including stated Chemical selling-price offset
metric.comparison: Calendar 2022 versus calendar 2021; exclude the FY2023 forecast bar

evidence.locator: Printed p. 23 / PDF page 23, Consumer Products material-price impact chart: FY2022 bar and -46.0 versus 2021 annotation; footnote on Chemical selling-price offsets

figures.name: Reported total cost of rolling electricity cuts
figures.basis: Company-reported total cost of load-shedding, meaning scheduled electricity interruptions. Not identified solely as diesel or a tariff increase.
figures.comparison: H1FY2023; prior corresponding period ZAR12 million

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and Grains/Milling & Baking paragraphs

figures.name: Prior-period total cost of rolling electricity cuts
figures.basis: Prior-period total outage cost as quoted by the issuer; not the stated current incremental energy cost.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and Grains/Milling & Baking paragraphs

figures.name: Reported incremental energy costs
figures.basis: Separate company-stated incremental energy-cost figure; definition is not reconciled with 76 minus 12. Do not silently replace it with ZAR64 million.
figures.comparison: Current versus corresponding prior period, issuer-stated basis

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and Grains/Milling & Baking paragraphs

ranking_policy: Only the pressure passage enters first-stage ranking. Geography, identity, actions, profit, figures, unknowns and later outcomes are display-only.
episode_boundary: One half-year observation within continuing input inflation and electricity constraints. FY2023 annual and later interim reports are continuing context, not separate cases. True episode boundaries are unknown.
comparison_limit: South Africa-led group, with export/international activities. Electricity interruption costs include operating under rolling cuts, not just a higher power tariff. Group gross margin differs from domestic or grain-segment operating margin.
unknowns: Why reported total outage costs of 76 million South African rand versus 12 million coexist with a stated incremental energy-cost figure of 48 million rand; the source provides no reconciliation. Do not equate these bases.
Separate amounts for wheat, maize, power tariffs, backup generation and lost production.
Individual effects of pricing and efficiency actions; group profit also reflects insurance proceeds and financing costs.
True episode boundaries and later results.

pressure.value: Wheat and maize input costs rose. Operating energy costs increased during rolling electricity cuts.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and Grains/Milling & Baking paragraphs

margin_or_profit.value: Group gross margin was 27.0%, compared with 29.2% a year earlier. This measures sales less cost of sales as a share of group sales; it is not the grain division’s operating margin.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and Grains/Milling & Baking paragraphs; income statement printed p. 5 / PDF page 7

other_drivers.value: The company also reported changes in product mix, insurance receipts and financing costs. Group sales volumes fell 1%, while domestic volumes were flat; these are shipment figures, not an independent measure of consumer demand.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and domestic segment discussion

response.value: Tiger Brands said it was pursuing cost savings and supply-chain efficiencies. It planned further efficiency and affordability work; these plans and company explanations do not establish that an action caused a profit result.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1, Overview; printed p. 3, Outlook / PDF pages 3 and 5

metric.name: Group gross margin
metric.basis: Group gross profit divided by group revenue, rounded to one decimal in commentary; gross profit is revenue less cost of sales. Not operating margin or a margin adjusted for insurance proceeds.
metric.scope: Tiger Brands consolidated group, including domestic and export/international operations

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1 / PDF page 3, Overview and Grains/Milling & Baking paragraphs; income statement printed p. 5 / PDF page 7
